reviews.review:
I had some fun while completing Space marine in ~9 hours, but the whole experience is filled with generic shooter gameplay that doesn't do anything particularly special. 

I would only recommend buying this game if you are a big fan of the Warhammer 40k universe and want to see the world in this game.

A tentative recommendation for fans of 40k and/or @ a discount.

This is an old game, with elements of classic arcade in level design and game play features. This translates into linear corridor style gameplay with fixed/scripted encounters that have to be overcome via the only means possible before the area is unlocked and player can progress forwards with the level. The levels blend seamlessly into one another with cutscenes dialogues and animations delivering characterbackground and plot elements between major events and chapter ends. The single player campaign relies on an autosave checkpoint system but once played the different chapters become available for replay directly from the menu.

SP levels include static defense against waves, i'll drive u shoot mobile defense, advance and clear (vast majority) and boss style arenas, and jumppack sections. There are 16 sections split across 6 chapters, which i completed within 12 hours as a casual gamer.

The game controls are simple and fairly responsive albeit a little clunky in design. Gun play is as expected 1 button to shoot another to zoom another to reload and some guns have an additional quirk or feature like charge up/overheat or delayed activation. The play carries 1 pistol, 1 bolter and upto 2 specialist weapons at any point with limited ammo and pickups through the levels on all but the pistol. Periodically through the mission one will find weapon caches where they can reconfigure their gear and resupply on ammo and grenades.

Melee combat is more complex 1 button to attack another to stun each weapon has its own combo animations and lastly a recharge health mechanic called execute which locks the player into a sychronised slow motion animation of varying lengths that recharges ones health a certain degree upon its completion (all enemies remain active during this time leaving the player incredibly vunerable). There are 4 melee weapons in single player, 1 of wich prevents the use of specialist weapons firing. 

The game feels like a console port at times, levels have invisible walls or ancle hieght impassable terrain giving one the impression of more freedom and better visuals. Certain points of the game have additional mechainics requiring one to spam a certain key or active the keys in sequence as prompted on screen. There is no jump feature as such but the inclusion of the jumppack as a mechanic means some levels/sections are more 3 dimensional by design. 

The graphics are functional, the faces of the characters being decent, while the armour texture and details is lacking when close up, namely dialogue scens. The levels convey the atmosphere, but won't have you stopping to take in the scenery much like some games do.

The music score and sound effects are all decent, or atleast not immediately irritating after hearing the same thing ad infinitum. The voice acting and audio logs one finds are also note worthy, and while the script isn't all that it is atleast consistently delivered with the characters remaining true to themselves throughout. For those that know 40K they'll understand when i say the Titus would have been more plausable as a Spacewolf than an Ultramarine.

The multiplayer is split into 2 aspects, PvP and PvE. They are however, somewhat empty at this time and requires using the autofinder so jumping on a pug game isn't easy but Steam intergration allows friend invites. Both modes can however, be launched without being filled meaning they can be self hosted as SP if one so desires. The gameplay and handling of weapons is slightly different in MP for balance reasons, as one might expect.

The multiplayer also has a cosmetic customisation and skills rewards system based on various unlocks through online gamplay. This adds incentive and rewards failure in addition to success helping new players find their feet against the better equipped and more experienced community. Alas these don't work in Sp, which is to relaint upon fixed animations to allow for customisation.

Played on I7, win10 64bit, GTX970, Keyboard n Mouse.

I loved this game.  I've always loved the 40K universe, and have played several games in that genre.  But this is the first time I've *really* felt like a Space Marine, or that I was *really* in that world.  Loved the action, loved the combat, loved the writing, loved the voice acting, loved the level design, animations, and so on.  

(full disclosure: I played on Easy level, because I'm an old man with slow reactions.  No idea how it plays on harder difficulties.)
They need more Warhammer 40k games like this. It gets repetative, but the story is excellent, the setting is excellent. I just wish the online wasn't dead.
